debug.empty.title: Nothing is being debugged
debug.empty.how: Use the buttons next to the file name above, click the bug next to a script, or press {keys}
debug.empty.noKeys: Use the buttons next to the file name above, or click the bug next to a script in the scripts window
debug.notFile: Open a JavaScript or TypeScript file to debug it
debug.output.inTerminal: program output goes to the terminal
debug.dirty: This file has unsaved changes — the program runs what is on disk
debug.unsaved.title: Unsaved changes
debug.unsaved.why: The program runs what is on disk. Not saved: {count} — breakpoints in these files will not match:
debug.unsaved.failed:
not saved, so nothing was started:
{files}
debug.foreign.adapter: Not a project file: text provided by the debugger
debug.foreign.gone: This debugger source is no longer available: the session that produced it has ended
settings.debug.openBrowser: When a debugged program prints a local address, open it in the browser under the debugger
settings.debug.serverReady: How the address is recognised in the output (regular expression, the first group is the address)
settings.debug.browser: Which browser (empty — installed Chrome; canary, dev, edge, or a path)
settings.debug.webRoot: Folder the dev server serves from, relative to the project (empty — the project root)
debug.edit.title: Breakpoint at {path}:{line}
debug.edit.condition.hint: stop only when true, e.g. n === 3
debug.edit.logMessage.hint: print instead of stopping: value is {n}
debug.console.notPaused: The program is not paused — nothing to evaluate in
debug.title.run: Run the open file without the debugger
debug.stuck: The program did not stop. Kill it with the skull button — until then nothing new starts.
